canonical_addressing: Public rule citations use Mandate N for stable active rule IDs and Pillar IV item N for engine protocols. IDs are not positional and need not be contiguous. Retired IDs are not reassigned. Edit the current contract in place; do not append historical directives or incident records.
description: Current generic requirements for the AI OS socket, compiled for agent guidance. Requirements are not proof of completed functionality, conformance or size targets. AGENTS.md and the delegated self-build contract carry the same active boundaries. Optional operational history is not shipped policy or acceptance evidence.

design_principles.summary: Agents deliver authorized engineering end-to-end; privacy, spending, destruction and evidence boundaries remain explicit.
design_principles.title: Autonomous by default

design_principles.summary: Verify current tool/workspace state and cite live receipts or other verified sources. Reject fabricated paths and invalid evidence trails.
design_principles.title: Grounded outputs

design_principles.summary: Expose real agent interactions, tool provenance and redacted traces. Persistent archives are audit-only, not truth authority.
design_principles.title: Traceable reasoning

design_principles.summary: Use measured parallelism on available hardware; short bounded locks are allowed and no particular concurrency library is required.
design_principles.title: Concurrency-first

design_principles.summary: Rust runtime, tooling and shipped implementation closure are requirements; remaining foreign paths are migration defects, not exemptions.
design_principles.title: Rust substrate

design_principles.summary: Discovery, safe defaults and agent repair remove required user configuration without inventing credentials or paid-service consent.
design_principles.title: Zero-config auto

design_principles.summary: A generic standards-protocol AI OS socket above the host OS, with concrete implementations admitted separately.
design_principles.title: Generic AI OS socket

design_principles.summary: Use verified native installation and provisioning; native Windows has no shell or emulation prerequisite.
design_principles.title: One-line install

design_principles.summary: Qualify isolated candidates locally, promote atomically and verify health/rollback. Production is never a development test instance.
design_principles.title: Release-only self-build

foundation_pillars.summary: Models never certify facts. Resolve citations through live receipts; uncited narrative fails when citable receipts exist. With nothing citable, expose No citations found and mark the answer unverified.
foundation_pillars.title: Truth

foundation_pillars.summary: Use live EvidenceSession, ToolReceipt and EvidenceRecord provenance. Missing or optional historical records are not acceptance evidence.
foundation_pillars.title: Evidence

foundation_pillars.summary: Install cluster membership identity atomically and recover interrupted first start. A damaged ban list refuses membership rather than becoming empty.
foundation_pillars.title: Swarm

foundation_pillars.summary: Maintain mission-scoped blackboard state with redacted, inspectable outcomes and honest missing-state recovery.
foundation_pillars.title: Blackboard

foundation_pillars.summary: Expose redacted real traces and provenance; audit archives are not truth authority. A task handle released without an outcome becomes ABANDONED. Keep active tasks and prune finished task listings oldest-first beyond 512.
foundation_pillars.title: Glass box

foundation_pillars.summary: Preserve cross-process locked HMAC-SHA256 audit append, one-write JSONL records, length-bound atomic tip checkpoints, and fail-closed verification of unreadable or non-UTF-8 input.
foundation_pillars.title: Audit

foundation_pillars.summary: Discover safe defaults under authorization. First-run host config uses compiled defaults, never a current-directory file; credentials and paid-service consent remain explicit.
foundation_pillars.title: Zero-config Auto

foundation_pillars.summary: Await safety/security before execution. Damaged or unreadable privacy_mode enforces local_only; mode changes persist atomically or fail visibly. Grants match exact resources, explicit * globs or children at a / boundary. local_only prevents sending prompts/embeddings off host/LAN regardless of provider name.
foundation_pillars.title: Governance-first

foundation_pillars.summary: Use capability registries and separately hosted implementations. Refuse damaged or unreadable MCP configuration during admission instead of replacing existing configured servers.
foundation_pillars.title: Pluggable

foundation_pillars.summary: Sandbox untrusted execution. Preflight every patched file and use a single transaction snapshot; report failed rollback honestly. Reserve transaction IDs on disk, persist snapshots atomically and return failures. Commit/abort only against the snapshotted workspace.
foundation_pillars.title: Sandbox

foundation_pillars.summary: Preserve canonical ports 9090–9094 plus one uniform offset; preserve relative ports and publish any allowed fallback.
foundation_pillars.title: Host contract

foundation_pillars.summary: Train only from labelled valid receipts at a real sample threshold; torn lines are not proof and unlabelable records do not stall a batch. Recover crash-orphans oldest-first, publish hash-bound active/last-known-good weights, escalate misses to reasoning and keep workspace reflex caches bounded.
foundation_pillars.title: Reflexes

foundation_pillars.summary: Verify downloads against publisher-provided SHA-256 and recheck recorded provenance on every cold load. When no digest exists, report structural validation only, never digest verification.
foundation_pillars.title: Provision

foundation_pillars.summary: Use measured concurrency with brief necessary locks and isolated blocking work; no mandated library or fully wait-free claim.
foundation_pillars.title: Concurrency-first

notes: **`global susi`** — background daemon bound to the host substrate (`~/.susi` / `SusiDirs::substrate_home`), not to a project folder. Owns ports, models, and lock state.
The CLI uses the caller's cwd as workspace context; workspace scoping is not an OS chroot.
Canonical installed binary: SusiDirs::substrate_home/bin/susi (susi.exe on Windows); only verified installation or qualified promotion writes it.

**Control plane** — `susi start` / `susi stop` / `susi restart` are deterministic host commands (never natural-language missions). `start` / `restart` wait until ports 9090–9094 answer and print the endpoints.
Per-port config fields stay documentation-only; accessors return the canonical base + `port_offset` (`SUSI_PORT_OFFSET` env wins). `SUSI_HOME` roots a fully isolated second instance.
Peer scouts must not bind 9092 — only the daemon owns the host-contract UDP port.

components.function: Agent-of-agents governance, orchestration and A2A capability contracts.
Release orchestration, compliance auditing and classified intent ingestion.
Authorized host maintenance, resource audit and implementation provisioning.

Observe recurring gaps, receipt staging and audit bottlenecks without claiming repair. Bound reflex attempts per intent; publish only compiled sandbox-tested candidates and report remaining functional gaps.

Persistent host owner of ports, models and locks. Whole-binary SHA-256 trust anchors update atomically and fail on read errors. Admission requires the persisted host token; gossip integrity and external egress remain fail-closed. Only explicit authorized commands provision external resources.
Typed loopback client for sandboxed native execution. Share one implementation through declared dependency edges; enforce execution budgets and plugin validation.

Use one compiled copy per shared crate through real Cargo edges in paths → error → config → core/sandbox → services → daemon order. Preserve local service fallback, local signing, shared status-aware bounded HTTP transport, uniform instance offsets and a single typed error model. No cross-crate source mounting or duplicate dependencies; implementation dependencies stay behind their owning facade.
Load built-in module metadata and report configured ports.
Prepare authorized implementation weights and tools under policy.
Report detected CPU, memory and acceleration capacity.
Enforce governance and destructive-action admission.
Redact credentials and prevent unauthorized exfiltration.
Observe recurring capability gaps; diagnosis is not a claim of implemented repair.
Verify MCP JSON-RPC endpoint contracts.
Discover candidate dependencies through package metadata under reuse and license policy.
Manage context and analyze the authorized workspace.
Recruit bounded, sanitized specialist-agent profiles.
Classify intent and route eligible deterministic reflexes under measured latency budgets.
Validate, compile and sandbox-probe a candidate before atomic hot-load. A successful probe does not prove intent correctness; a diagnostic fallback leaves the functional gap open and reports why.
Host supported local inference through admitted implementations; preserve honest format and hardware support reporting.
Route eligible local/cloud or explicit inference choices under one placement policy with auditable decision IDs.
Load validated local reflex weights with active/last-known-good provenance.
Discover, configure, prefer and probe admitted coding-model implementations.
Discover, configure, prefer and probe admitted reasoning-model implementations.
Discover, provision, prefer and probe admitted open-weight implementations.
Compatibility entry for a separately configured model-routing implementation; preserve credentials, prefer pins and live capability probing.
Enable, disable and probe MCP implementations through durable extensible configuration.
Discover, diagnose, configure and run external agent/framework capabilities through the socket.
Serve host-contract MCP Streamable HTTP on 9090 with /mcp and /messages compatibility, HTTP alias 9093 and discovery on 9092.
Provide a CLI protocol bridge.
Serve inference HTTP on canonical 9091 plus the uniform instance offset. Allowed unpinned whole-block fallback is logged and published; pinned conflicts fail closed.
GAWD capability preserving ACP discovery, JSON-RPC/HTTP, SSE and stdio NDJSON negotiation, prompt/turn streaming, cancellation, capability admission and pinned conformance contracts.
Compose drivers/engines and parallel isolated workers with resource admission, remote reconciliation and serialized integration.
Mint mission-scoped live tool receipts and require verifiable citations.
Accept verified live receipts, compiled reads and native verified evidence; models never certify facts.
Represent structured claims and sources verified against the live receipt ledger.
Maintain redacted runtime provenance with bounded resident memory, identity-bound replay and atomic compaction; optional history does not grow checked-out source.

Keep external implementation dependencies behind their owning facade, with caller-owned URL/SSRF, privacy and resource policy. A facade is not license or Rust-closure evidence; generic socket APIs preserve compatibility during destination-first extraction.

body.name: Capability inventory
body.subtitle: Compatibility symbols and responsibilities; implementation listings are not qualification evidence

mandates.title: Truth and current evidence
mandates.imperative: Report actual outcomes, failures and limitations. Verify facts, paths and APIs before asserting them and recheck mutable state before acting. Fresh source and empirical results outrank memory or model belief. Mission completion needs live EvidenceSession/ToolReceipt citations, compiled reads or native verified receipts; models never certify facts. Missing history is unverified, never proof.

mandates.title: Client acknowledgment budget
mandates.imperative: Require client acknowledgment within 2ms through acknowledgment, streaming or a background handle. Measure acknowledgment separately from inference, I/O and mission completion; do not apply the acknowledgment ceiling to total mission time. Keep primitive operations sub-millisecond where feasible.

mandates.title: Bounded concurrency
mandates.imperative: Prefer non-blocking channels, atomics and sharded structures on the swarm path; keep necessary locks brief and isolate bounded blocking work from asynchronous critical paths. No library is mandated and no fully wait-free guarantee is implied. Respect dependency and resource ceilings.

mandates.title: Critical evaluation
mandates.imperative: Critically evaluate code, architecture, evidence and logic; report defects and unresolved gaps plainly.

mandates.title: Technical communication
mandates.imperative: Use professional, precise technical prose in code, documentation and reports. Style goals are review criteria, not mechanically proven absence of every subjective defect.

mandates.title: Credential protection
mandates.imperative: Never expose credentials or sensitive configuration in source, logs, telemetry, mission traces or outbound tool content. Redact configured secret-token patterns before durable writes while preserving surrounding inspectable records. Mask environment credentials in error metrics. Veto actions carrying held *_API_KEY, *_TOKEN or *_SECRET values independently of known prefixes. Token patterns match token starts, not embedded word fragments. Detection is configuration-based; unknown formats are not proven safe.

mandates.title: Functional production paths
mandates.imperative: Ship working capabilities without silent mocks, placeholders or fake success. Clearly labelled test fixtures and doubles remain permitted. Diagnose unavailable capabilities honestly and preserve acceptance criteria.

mandates.title: Bounded resource authority
mandates.imperative: Use measured CPU/GPU and memory capacity without OOM or oversubscription. Hardware capacity does not override rate limits, bearer authorization, policy, evidence, spending limits or operator preferences.

mandates.title: Persistent host service
mandates.imperative: Maintain a resilient background service bound to the host substrate, owning the 9090–9094 host-contract block, models and lock state. Never silently remap individual ports.

mandates.title: Policy-gated provisioning
mandates.imperative: Select compatible weights using detected capacity and configured rankings, respecting prefer pins, offline/no-download controls, disk limits, licenses and authorization. Provisioning is best-effort; missing permission or resources cannot be reported as success.

mandates.title: Registry refresh
mandates.imperative: Validate dynamic agent-registry timestamps and reload changes without admitting stale or unvalidated behavior.

mandates.title: Governed adaptation
mandates.imperative: Adapt runtime structure and agent composition from empirical outcomes. Registry refresh, reflex synthesis and mission feedback remain subordinate to safety, security, untrusted-input checks, destructive-action authorization and evidence requirements.

mandates.title: Useful decomposition
mandates.imperative: Run separable subtasks in parallel and join their results when beneficial. Use sequential or single-agent execution when appropriate; parallelism is not an unconditional requirement.

mandates.title: Honest recovery
mandates.imperative: Keep required live mission checkpoints and receipts in runtime state for recovery and diagnosis. Recovery coverage is path-dependent; missing checkpoints never justify a claim of resumed success. Optional operational history may be absent and must not accumulate in source.

mandates.title: Decoupled messaging
mandates.imperative: Prefer asynchronous channels for multi-agent orchestration. Short synchronous local calls remain appropriate when a channel adds overhead without benefit.

mandates.title: Verified evolution order
mandates.imperative: Self-modification follows triggering intent, architecture, implementation and verification, in that order. Changes to production additionally require the independent release-qualification and promotion sequence.

mandates.title: Dynamic intent admission
mandates.imperative: Resolve intents through dynamic registries, configuration and capability contracts for extensions, agents, tools, models and peers. Core admission must not depend on a closed domain-specific goal enumeration.

mandates.title: Bounded recovery and port ownership
mandates.imperative: Recover eligible runtime faults and reclaim ports only from a verified stale instance under destructive-action guards. Preserve the relative host-contract block: a foreign owner with a pinned offset fails closed; an unpinned daemon may select the first free offset in steps of 100, logging and publishing the result in ports.json. Never silently drift to ephemeral per-port alternatives.

mandates.title: Generic protocol socket
mandates.imperative: Keep domain and provider implementations outside the generic core socket. Admit local and remote engines, tools and agents through standard protocols and configuration while preserving existing wire, import, error and refusal compatibility until implementation migration is verified.

mandates.title: Core license
mandates.imperative: Core is available under Apache-2.0 as specified in LICENSE. Preserve required license, copyright, patent, attribution and modification notices; licensing is not a claim of behavioral compliance.

mandates.title: Destructive-action authorization
mandates.imperative: Before any destructive filesystem, Git or process operation, apply SafetyDetector command and critical-system-path checks and require explicit, unambiguous authorized intent. Incidental keywords in free-text goals cannot trigger mutation or destruction. Audit every execution-capable path, including internal administration; SafetyAgent enforces the veto.

mandates.title: Redacted observability
mandates.imperative: Expose real actions, tool calls, state changes and outcomes through mission traces, blackboards, governance reports and receipt provenance. Redact credentials before persistence without hiding the surrounding event. Audit archives do not confer truth authority; use live evidence. Do not claim access to private model internals or universal transparency.

mandates.title: Action attribution
mandates.imperative: Give each operator-visible or audited action a unique attribution to its agent, tool call, receipt or reflex. Reflexes are one attribution class, not the identity of every action.

mandates.title: Host and workspace scope
mandates.imperative: The persistent host service owns ports, models and locks under SusiDirs::substrate_home. The canonical CLI uses cwd as mission context and applies workspace edits transactionally. Workspace scoping is not an OS chroot or a claim that every process is sandboxed to cwd. Network surfaces retain independent authentication.

mandates.title: Progress, cancellation and leases
mandates.imperative: Client surfaces acknowledge, stream or return a background handle without waiting for full completion. Enforce cancellation and execution leases before client timeouts. Category idle leases use five times the worst observed progress gap, floored by execution_lease_secs, only after three completed samples. Persist calibration atomically; report lost or malformed calibration as an error. Progress must be observed output, never a synthetic timer heartbeat.

mandates.title: Versioned private candidates
mandates.imperative: Synchronize version manifests and build identified candidates in private state. A source edit, version bump or binary signature never authorizes production replacement. Preserve the running builder and previous verified artifact; report toolchain and network failures.

mandates.title: Capability control planes
mandates.imperative: Preserve orchestration, local/cloud inference placement, model provisioning, agent/framework and MCP control-plane capabilities through generic contracts and separately hosted implementations. Respect supported formats, resumable downloads, operator choices and policy. Catalog contents are implementation data, not fixed core policy; never provision subscriptions implicitly.

mandates.title: Extensible configuration
mandates.imperative: Admit models, providers, agents, tools and servers through registries, traits and runtime configuration without editing closed core enums. User-editable configuration, including nested typed convenience structures, preserves unknown fields through read-modify-write. Fixed wire/telemetry shapes may remain closed. The canonical 9090–9094 ports plus uniform offset are intentional compatibility constants.

mandates.title: Governance before execution
mandates.imperative: Dispatch and await SafetyAgent and SecurityAgent before any execution-capable agent in the same mission. Governance and execution must never race in one parallel batch.

mandates.title: Outbound controls
mandates.imperative: Check outbound action text against configured exfiltration-vector patterns before execution, independently of credential-pattern and held-secret checks. Preserve URL, destination and privacy restrictions.

mandates.title: Fail-closed HTTP admission
mandates.imperative: Network-facing HTTP requires configured bearer authentication and per-client rate limits before route dispatch, except CORS preflight and unauthenticated liveness. Seed api_auth_token securely into a mode-0600 api_token using exclusive creation so a concurrent persisted token wins. Reject symlink/non-regular, empty or unreadable token paths, failed entropy and I/O failures; bind no host ports and spawn no leaf service or cell without the persisted token. No weak in-memory fallback. Before seeding, deny non-loopback peers; once configured, localhost also needs the bearer. Bucket IPv6 clients by /64 and mapped IPv6 as IPv4.

mandates.title: Untrusted intent and generated state
mandates.imperative: Treat externally sourced goals and derived tool arguments, descriptions and blackboard entries as untrusted. Every mutating or destructive operation needs an explicit intent sentinel; admin pulse: is the administrative example. Before persisting or reusing synthesized profiles, bound fields, force is_core=false and apply governance checks.

mandates.title: Recoverable errors
mandates.imperative: Production I/O, state and IPC propagate typed Result/EaiResult errors instead of panicking. Preserve poison recovery and pre-epoch time fallback. Production panic-path macros are denied; test-only fixture allowances remain scoped and justified.

mandates.title: AI OS boundary
mandates.imperative: Provide a generic AI OS socket above the host OS: GAWD, GEMI and GMCP coordinate local/remote capabilities under budgets, privacy, evidence and audit contracts. Do not claim to replace the host kernel, init, package manager or desktop. Credentials remain operator-owned; placement decisions retain signed audit attribution. Gossip uses per-peer MACs and fails closed without a key; NAT egress remains policy-gated and relay allocation authenticates integrity. Background version probes are not authorization for live cloud provisioning. Source self-modification and production promotion remain separately gated.

mandates.title: Authorized autonomous delivery
mandates.imperative: Agents own planning, implementation, testing, debugging, integration and qualification end-to-end without asking the requester to inspect code or perform routine engineering. Use isolated parallel workers where useful. Preserve user scope and stop instructions, credentials, privacy, spending, destructive-action authorization and safety/security/truth gates. Missing evidence or failed checks cannot be COMPLETE.

mandates.title: Native installation
mandates.imperative: Use native Rust installation and provisioning with verified artifact hashes, native paths and automatic discovery. Support verified installation and native source builds without a hosting-service prerequisite. Windows must need no Bash, WSL, MSYS, Python, Node or container. Preserve production, download/spending authorization and diagnosable failures; demonstrate clean-machine success. Legacy scripts remain migration debt.

mandates.title: Qualified installed release
mandates.imperative: Keep installed production separate from private development candidates; it changes only through qualified promotion and does not build its own successor. Keep it current when a newer release is qualified for this host, reachable and no client is mid-mission. Verify the release record, source-built host artifact and digest before atomic update; retain rollback and report updater failures. Private targets, homes, ports, credentials and daemon lifecycles never overwrite or test against production. A compilation, debug build, tag or model statement is not production authorization.

mandates.title: Isolated worktree delivery
mandates.imperative: Each agent uses its own worktree, branch, identity, build output and runtime state. Reserve disjoint scopes and integrate serially against the current head, preserving dirty and accepted work. Use available cargo local-workflow reservations and guarded commits; implement missing behavior rather than claiming it. Main is unqualified development without mandatory pre-push gates; release candidates need exact combined-tree acceptance. Never force-push, delete main, overwrite shared history or bypass live controls. Canonical instruction entry points point to AGENTS.md.

mandates.title: Scoped task ownership
mandates.imperative: Keep unique task identifiers, dependencies, scopes and meaningful acceptance in active/local task state, with one live claim per worker. Reservations are atomic and reject overlap including native path aliases; cross-host work uses a shared coordinator. Attribute guarded commits with Task: T-<AGENT>-<n> or the native Task: LOCAL-<name> receipt. A receipt or compile is not acceptance. Close only after nonempty checks pass on the actual integrated tree; partial success cannot close broader goals. Preserve unfinished work through crash/recovery. Completed task history need not remain in source. Keep active task records truthful, readable and duplicate-free, with goal, size and acceptance. Close through acceptance; retire unwanted work with its reason. An open record cannot say done/failed/canceled; review untouched, unclaimed tasks after 14 days.

mandates.title: Concurrent state integrity
mandates.imperative: Reserve disjoint edits and private writable worktrees, targets, homes and ports. Validate structured state natively; inspect staged, unstaged, untracked and renamed paths. Serialize integration against the current head and test the combined tree. Preserve others' active work and accepted changes; a textual merge is not behavioral proof. Growing optional records belong in local storage, not source; absence is never acceptance evidence.

mandates.title: Hermetic verification
mandates.imperative: Tests use private HOME/USERPROFILE/XDG/SUSI_HOME, configuration, ports and local remotes with credentials scrubbed. Never read or mutate production state or shared development homes. Synchronize and restore process-global environment changes. Share only validated read-only toolchain/dependency caches. Prove fixture routing and unchanged production; network tests require explicit classification and provisioning. Do not send real coordination messages from tests.

mandates.title: Exact native release evidence
mandates.imperative: Qualify a clean identified candidate with the locked graph, license and Rust-source audits, formatting, clippy, nonempty required tests, freshly built executable smoke tests including applicable E2E_CHECKS, artifact digest and provenance. Bind proof to exact source, lockfile, compiler, target and features. Promote atomically with health checks and verified rollback. Immutable release records retain required provenance independently of optional history; tags never replace proof. A failed gate blocks promotion, not repair.

mandates.title: Integrated release gate
mandates.imperative: Qualify the actual combined release tree. Main publication is unqualified development, not this gate. Serialize release publication and compare-and-swap the head; missing/stale proof, conflicts or failures fail closed while preserving work. Hosted checks, pull requests and remote review neither replace nor constitute the native gate.

mandates.title: Commands and mission admission
mandates.imperative: Refuse command-shaped or flag-shaped argv before inference spending, daemon startup or evidence writes; return exit 2 with a valid command-path suggestion. Only prose intent enters mission routing. Keep new commands discoverable by this guard and cover refusals with executable smoke checks. Never submit a command-shaped string hoping mission inference will run it.

mandates.title: Outcome-ranked inference
mandates.imperative: Choose providers per task class from measured outcomes and latency, with privacy, spending and cooldown filters before ranking; prefer local as the floor and eligible cloud as the ceiling. Fold mission outcomes once as non-citable brain:* receipts. Quarantine rejected-key/no-credit scopes on the 10min/1h/6h ladder, rank healthy providers ahead of recent failures, and recover preferences when healthy. Never remove or disable keys because a call failed. Cost tiers inform ranking without overriding evidence; expose the decision.

mandates.title: Credential budget isolation
mandates.imperative: Mask BYOK previews, preserve tenant/credential scope and optional max_budget_usd ceilings. Atomically account for spend before inference dispatch and quarantine exhausted credentials until authorized clearing or top-up. Delegation cannot increase spending authority.

mandates.title: Protocol conformance and admission
mandates.imperative: Preserve the pinned MCP/GMCP specifications and complete tool, prompt, completion, resource, task and server lifecycle contracts. Evaluate poisoning, prompt injection, changed-tool and exfiltration defenses before execution or session registration. Requirements are not a certification claim; demonstrate conformance with executed tests.

mandates.title: Auditable unsafe boundaries
mandates.imperative: Keep forbid(unsafe_code) in substrate, transport, client and library crates and deny(unsafe_code) for necessary native FFI. Exceptions are narrowly scoped per function or metadata item with SAFETY reasoning, ownership and lifecycle checks; no module-wide allowance or raw-handle leakage. Deny unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn and production panic-path macros. Native verification enforces these boundaries.

mandates.title: Dependency ownership
mandates.imperative: Ordinary susi-* crates declare no external normal/build/dev/target dependencies. Every external dependency has one susi-vendor-* owner; consumers use its facade. Preserve leaf dependency order and auditability, avoid duplicate declarations and source mounts, and do not hide foreign implementation behind a Rust facade.

mandates.title: Complete native agent loop
mandates.imperative: The harness owns planning, scoped claims, isolated workers, budgets, feedback, serialized integration, release qualification and closure. Delegate current AGENTS.md and susi_core::self_build::BRIEF constraints. Main remains unqualified development without mandatory pre-push gates. Missing native capabilities remain explicit work; they never justify requiring requester code review, weakening release gates or changing access controls.

mandates.title: Measured end-to-end delivery
mandates.imperative: Authorized agents may commit, push and merge scoped work without routine approval, preserving isolation and serialized integration. This grants no unrelated spending, destructive authority or external publication. The delivery goal stays open until a real source change reaches a verified live executable in under 60 seconds with declared millisecond response budgets. Measure cold/warm build, tests, startup, acknowledgment, first output and completion separately, from change-ready through integration, promotion and observed behavior; include repetitions, failures and rollback. Preserve simple public protocols and conformance tests for permissions, discovery, errors and compatibility. Demonstrate implementation-package updates over the socket without rebuilding core, preserving capabilities and measuring source, dependencies, artifact size and wall time. Wrap scoped work at 10% weekly allowance remaining; source publication is not qualification.

mandates.title: Rust implementation closure
mandates.imperative: Runtime, build, install, integration and release tooling plus shipped dependencies must be Rust; Rust-produced Wasm is allowed. Audit build scripts, linked objects, assets and helpers for each supported target/profile/features. Inventory OS ABI and compiler/linker boundaries without hiding foreign runtimes. A facade, optional label or downloaded binary is not proof. Preserve capabilities during replacement. Thin Git hook shell stubs may only locate and run native tooling; other scripts remain shrinking migration debt, with no new scripts.

mandates.title: Native platform qualification
mandates.imperative: Core releases qualify Linux only; Windows qualification uses native x86_64 MSVC with native services, processes, paths and updates, without shell/emulation/container prerequisites. Exercise clean-machine setup, drive/UNC and Unicode paths, reserved names, junctions, locking, interruption and atomic promotion. Actual native artifacts/tests are required; cross-compilation and inspection alone are insufficient. Git's own thin native-tool hook handoff is the compatibility boundary.

mandates.title: Measured parallel delivery
mandates.imperative: Schedule independent scopes concurrently within measured capacity using private identities, worktrees, targets, homes and ports. Serialize integration/publication, preserve work on conflict/crash and use normal fast-forward updates against the current head. Validate shared immutable caches. Measure cold/warm cost, queue contention, throughput and resources; never remove release checks or oversubscribe to manufacture speed.

mandates.title: Portable local development
mandates.imperative: Planning through production qualification must work locally without hosting-service accounts, APIs, hosted CI, pull requests or remote claims. Use portable Git storage and reproducible dependency provenance. Offline checks account for build-script downloads as well as package resolution. Document and test cold provisioning; a warm cache alone proves no cold-machine capability.

mandates.title: Atomic production promotion
mandates.imperative: Keep debug and optimized candidates distinct from installed production. Before promotion qualify exact source, policy, tests, executable smoke checks, digest and provenance. Retain the previous verified artifact, atomically replace, verify health and roll back on failure. Test interruption and native file-lock behavior. Version strings, compile-only results, scope receipts and tags are not release attestations.

mandates.title: Complete license obligations
mandates.imperative: Distributed dependencies allow Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-2-Clause and BSD-3-Clause under the deny policy. All AND obligations must comply; an allowed OR grant must actually exist; exceptions are not silently accepted. Audit transitive code, build/runtime helpers, model/tokenizer assets and linked objects, preserving notices and attribution. Never relabel, exclude shipped components or widen policy to pass. Platform boundaries are not loopholes and protocol peers are not compliance proof. Copied/ported source requires the narrower pure Apache-2.0 grant.

mandates.title: Measured size and cost
mandates.imperative: Remove dead paths, duplicates, unnecessary dependencies/features, speculative frameworks and mandatory service bloat while preserving required capabilities. Track artifact/distribution size, idle memory, startup, latency and cold/warm builds. BloatAuditor continuously checks dead code, oversized functions and behavior/config drift without certifying every byte necessary. Existing vendor, dependency, unsafe and size ratchets only tighten. Keep the warm build+test+release target under 10s and cold compile target under 60s, distinct from full qualification.

mandates.title: Zero required user configuration
mandates.imperative: Use discovery, safe defaults and agent repair for installation, first run, local/cloud routing, scheduling, isolation and updates. Preserve deliberate choices. Credentials, privacy consent, paid services and spending caps remain explicit; never invent, scrape or purchase credentials. Missing services or permissions fail visibly. Demonstrate clean-machine, upgrade and offline behavior before claiming the default path needs no user configuration.

mandates.title: Demonstrated improvement
mandates.imperative: Tie an upgrade to reproducible goal/baseline evidence, identified source/dependencies/compiler, correctness, resource measurements and the integrated artifact. Promote only demonstrated improvement without forbidden regressions and retain verified rollback. Store required verifiable learning outcomes durably outside source; embeddings and model assertions are not proof or permanent memory.

mandates.title: Publication and implementation boundary
mandates.imperative: Core remains Apache-2.0, free to fork and published one way. Only the designated publisher holds push authority; authorized agents exercise it within scope without granting new access. Accept no outside pull request, patch or commit. License rights do not grant the Susi name or marks. Keep proprietary source out of core. Generic socket contracts stay in core; concrete implementations, UI and add-on packages belong outside and may migrate there after destination-first compatibility proof. Preserve separate implementation licensing and signatures, including SUSI-ENT-v1 and Ed25519 SUSI-CUST-v1 where applicable. Qualify only native x86_64 Windows/Linux, retaining portable source without adding other platform build/test/release legs. Use no hosted CI.

mandates.title: Composable agents and serialized integration
mandates.imperative: Authorized local/cloud drivers and engines compose across container components through versioned capability contracts. Enforce cycle detection, termination/cancellation, resource/time/depth limits and traceable evidence; nested work cannot amplify permissions. Use measured capacity, not fixed agent or push-rate limits. Distill labelled features and reconcile remote changes at workflow boundaries. Main is unqualified development without mandatory pre-push gates; release lines need exact-tree qualification and immutable tags. Preserve confidentiality, authorization, production health and rollback. Default-driver status requires measured parity.

mandates.title: Fast pipeline and portable publication
mandates.imperative: Measure warm build_ms, test_ms, release_ms and total_ms under the 10,000ms target, reporting cold and warm separately. The focused fast-release pipeline is not full qualification. Keep commits scoped and attributable with Task/Feature/Depends and applicable Harvest/Origin trailers in active/local state. Fetch and merge origin/main before starting, resuming and each commit when reachable; report offline failures, preserve dirty work and resolve conflicts without rebasing shared history. Publish only refs/heads/main as a branch, refs/agents/<agent> for handoffs and fast-forward refs/candidates/release/<name> for qualification; release tags are immutable. Atomically publish against the current head and retry lost races. Use portable Git, not hosting APIs or hosted checks.

mandates.title: Verified source intake
mandates.imperative: Quarantine upstream source without executing it. Copy or port only pure Apache-2.0, or an explicitly available and elected Apache-2.0 OR alternative; refuse other grants, AND obligations and exceptions unless pure Apache-2.0 is separately available. Pin commits, verify per-file rights and preserve section 4 license, attribution and modification notices, harvest manifests and Origin trailers. Route generic primitives within core ceilings and concrete products to separate implementation packages. Never import proprietary source into core. First-contact contributions and external messages need explicit authorization.

mandates.title: Authorized coordination
mandates.imperative: Read relevant coordination state before claiming, integrating and publishing; respect scoped stops and other owners. Use the authorized shared coordination surface, report truthful claims/results without secrets or private source, and resolve conflicts directly. External messages require explicit user or invoked-workflow authorization. Coordination notes are not acceptance evidence or a gate added to main; no hosting-service dependency is required.

mandates.title: Owned agent roots
mandates.imperative: Each agent uses one registered root per machine, with an owner marker; register existing roots in place. Roots never nest or overlap. Keep owned source, worktrees, targets, runtime homes, logs and scratch beneath that root. Never edit, move or delete another root or the requester's working directory. Read/fetch is allowed; coordinate needed changes with the owner within messaging authorization. Shared tools/remotes remain shared and must not be changed without applicable authority.

mandates.title: Reuse before implementation
mandates.imperative: Inspect both repositories, suitable Apache-2.0 source/services and the locked dependency graph before adding code. Reuse only needed parts, delete replaced duplicates, and preserve Rust, safety, license and size/cost bounds. Audit copied source under pure Apache-2.0 intake rules; existing tools do not authorize foreign shipped dependencies. Record the search, decision and build reason in active/local task state before committing feature work. A recorded search is not proof it was thorough.

mandates.title: Current goals and learning
mandates.imperative: Keep current goals in bounded active/local state and revisit unfulfilled goals and changed upstream dependencies. Import only changes serving an authorized goal under reuse, license and destination rules. Upstream movement invites review, not automatic intake. Optional completed history may be absent; never append source histories to retain growing facts. Missing records prove no completion, and improvement grants no extra authority or release exemption.

mandates.title: Three core pillars
mandates.imperative: Keep exactly GAWD, GEMI and GMCP. A2A, ACP and the parallel harness are GAWD capabilities; retain public endpoint/import compatibility. Keep source, tests and current contract consistent across implementation boundaries. Review ready work for safe integration about every ten minutes, preserving ownership and reconciling current main. Never force incomplete/conflicted merges or assert unmeasured speed, standards conformance or completed size goals.

mandates.title: Qualified host release synchronization
mandates.imperative: A release qualified for the current host is complete only after the installed binary, susi.build.json and live daemon match it and pass health checks. Preserve the previous verified binary and roll back failures. Verify qualified artifact SHA-256 and version before reuse, without redundant rebuild. Unqualified binaries are refused. Every Windows scheduled task retains RunLevel=Limited so ordinary process visibility and stop/swap authority remain available. Report installed/qualified/latest drift and repair authorized updates.

mandates.title: Meaningful ten-minute cadence
mandates.imperative: Commit, push, merge and pull about every ten minutes during active work, in addition to start/resume/precommit synchronization. This is a drift-reduction cadence, not a hard deadline or a new main gate. Publish meaningful steps only; no empty commits, noise or broken work to satisfy a clock. Pull means fetch and merge, never shared-history rebase or force. Resolve conflicts; report unreachable remotes honestly.

mandates.title: Agent operating boundaries
mandates.imperative: Work independently on useful tasks while dependencies are pending, collaborate within authorization and retain isolated ownership. Renew active claims; release when work stops. Use only the authorized automation vault or scoped process environment, never a private personal vault, and never expose secret values. Full engineering autonomy grants no harmful, destructive, spending or unrelated publication authority; delegated permissions only narrow. Bring a fix or a concrete scoped task with a problem.

mandates.title: Strict core size goal
mandates.imperative: The complete socket must be strictly below 10,000 physical runtime Rust lines, including every platform/feature, blanks, comments, inline tests and susi-vendor-* facades under docs/lean-core.md. Until met, core never grows; any runtime addition is paid for in the same change. Lower COMPLETE_SOCKET_CEILING after reductions and retain 9,999 as the maximum once below target. No minification, hidden excluded runtime, capability loss or weakened protocol/security acceptance. Only explicit user authority may change the limit. Keep runtime/current docs generic while preserving protocol identifiers and mandatory attribution.

mandates.title: Release inactive claims
mandates.imperative: Release ownership in the same step work completes, is handed off, abandoned or stops. Never reserve idle work for later or wait for lease expiry; the lease is a last resort. Completed accepted tasks reserve no scope even if a stale record remains. Preserve or explicitly abandon unpublished work; list and release finished claims before leaving. Optional completed task records need not stay in source.

mandates.title: Safe finished-worktree cleanup
mandates.imperative: Remove only an owned worktree and merged branch/private target when every commit is on origin/main, the tree is clean, no live claim or running agent owns it and the next task is not reusing it. Recheck immediately before removal. Never remove primary/requester checkouts, another agent's work, unpublished changes or shared caches. Preserve or deliberately abandon unpublished work first; reuse an eligible worktree for the next task instead of keeping idle reserves.

mandates.title: Tidy authorized coordination
mandates.imperative: When shared messaging is authorized, close items by appending closures rather than editing/deleting entries. Close owned requests/claims, answer addressed requests and report each fact once. Only the originator or an authorized decision lifts a stop. A request with no reply may close after two days only if both parties have also been silent for two days; an expired claim may close after two days. Before leaving, reconcile authorized entries and release claims and eligible worktrees. This policy supplies no external-message authorization.

protocols.imperative: Use private worktrees, targets, runtime homes and ports. Preserve production and other workers; verify hermetic routing before side effects.
protocols.title: Workspace Purity

protocols.imperative: Use measured hardware capacity without exceeding memory, policy, authorization, rate or spending limits.
protocols.title: Hardware Saturation

protocols.imperative: Identify a clean candidate and locked graph; audit licenses and Rust closure; run formatting, clippy and nonempty required tests; build and smoke-test the executable in isolation; bind digest to source/compiler/target/features; atomically promote, verify health and roll back failures. Each step gates the next; publication is not qualification.
protocols.title: Motion Rule (Release Gate)

protocols.imperative: Use conventional commit prefixes and no emoji in commit messages.
protocols.title: Conventional Reflex

protocols.imperative: Prefer verified already-qualified artifacts when available, with native source-build fallback. Verify hashes and qualification before deployment.
protocols.title: Binary Dominance

protocols.imperative: Make the canonical installed binary discoverable through the native host PATH without overwriting unrelated settings.
protocols.title: Auto-Path Injection

protocols.imperative: Only verified installation or qualified release promotion writes the canonical host binary. CLI invocations retain workspace context and consult the substrate lock to avoid duplicate daemons. Reload a verified canonical replacement, preserve ports/models and verify health/rollback. Development candidates run separately and never write production.
protocols.title: Canonical Binary Dynamics & Hot-Reload Protocol

steps.imperative: Stage validated intents through non-blocking ingestion.
steps.title: Pulse Ingestion

steps.imperative: Construct the execution graph and recruit authorized sanitized specialists under resource budgets; await safety/security before execution.
steps.title: Swarm Synthesis

steps.imperative: Require live receipt citations, compiled reads or native verified evidence at convergence. Model review is not a completion path.
steps.title: Truth Convergence

steps.imperative: The host owns hardware, ports, locks and policy-gated provisioning. The CLI confines mission edits to the selected workspace through transactions; this is not an OS chroot. Source development uses private candidates and exact-tree release qualification before production promotion.
